existing_copy_for_context_only.long: Inkombank’s collapse is the event documented in the linked timeline. It says the Russian Central Bank revoked the bank’s license on October 29, 1998, after the bank had been taken over by Semion Mogilevich in 1994. The failure was initially attributed to management decisions during Russia’s financial crisis. The timeline later connects it to a suspected money-laundering scheme and cites a 2001 Moscow testimony in which a former bank member said management had secretly removed about $1 billion from the bank’s assets. It also says Inkombank was a major commercial partner of the Bank of New York and that managers of the two banks traveled between Moscow and New York. existing_copy_for_context_only.medium: On February 17, 1999, Evercore Partners acquired American Media, publisher of the National Enquirer and Star, and David Pecker became the company’s chairman and CEO. This was a change in ownership at the parent company, not a personal purchase of the Enquirer by Pecker. The transaction does not establish the paper’s earlier Mafia financing claims.
existing_copy_for_context_only.long: On February 17, 1999, Evercore Partners acquired American Media Inc., the publisher of the National Enquirer and Star. Evercore was led by Roger Altman, and David Pecker, then an executive at Hachette Filipacchi, was hired to lead American Media as chairman and chief executive. The transaction changed control of the parent publisher and put Pecker in charge of its publications; it was not a personal purchase of the Enquirer by Pecker. The distinction matters because the title describes a different buyer and a separate claim about the paper’s earlier history. This transaction record does not establish whether the National Enquirer had previously received Mafia financing, and the 1999 acquisition itself is not reported as involving Donald Trump. Pecker’s later relationship with Trump should not be projected backward onto the purchase. The reported event is Evercore’s acquisition of American Media and Pecker’s appointment to run the company.
